purpose: Machine-readable audit contract for finding genuinely weak content owners, distinguishing them from intentionally concise schemas/registries, and prioritizing consolidation before file multiplication.
interpretation: Depth is a function of role, explanatory substance, relationships, evidence routing and reader value—not byte size alone. A 1 KB registry can be healthy; a 3 KB first-class concept owner can be underdeveloped.

categories.stub: identifier or nearly empty substantive record
categories.label: name and short description only
categories.metadata: structured fields without enough explanatory substance
categories.deep: substantive plus dense relationships, questions and evidence/source architecture
categories.corpus: deep source record backed by reusable primary text and stable passage structure
categories.control: schema/index/registry/router whose intended job is concise structure rather than explanatory content

file_roles.first-class-owner: High-connectivity concept/branch owner; should usually be substantive or deep.
file_roles.substantive-owner-or-dataset: Domain content intended to answer questions or preserve reusable evidence.
file_roles.developmental-or-recovery: Wave/addendum/recovery stratum; can remain separate while historically useful, but should be promoted and retired when fully superseded.
file_roles.evidence-ledger: May be repetitive by design; quality is provenance/coverage rather than prose depth.
file_roles.routing-or-ledger: Index/navigation layer; should be concise but accurate and reachable.
file_roles.control-or-routing: Schema, registry, backend, manifest, checklist or completion contract; brevity is often correct.

automatic_checks: all IDs unique where the schema requires uniqueness
all relationship endpoints resolve or are explicitly unresolved research endpoints
all registered local source paths exist
no imported-and-verified text points only to an external URL
major index entries expose useful local content and source trails
placeholder language is flagged rather than treated as substance
first-class owners are penalized more strongly for shallow content than routing/control files
wave/addendum files are reviewed for promotion into durable owners
retired-file references are removed from active readers and routers
upgrade_rule: Upgrade the highest-connectivity shallow records first. If unique information already belongs to an existing owner, enrich that owner and retire the redundant satellite rather than creating another file.
consolidation_rule: Before deleting any file: identify unique information, choose the durable owner, migrate the unique information, migrate inbound references, preserve provenance/consolidation history where useful, then delete only when no independent source role remains.
thin_by_design_examples: knowledge/indexes/* when used purely for routing

Project canon versus comparative philosophical/theological context.
Distinct registry, integrity-contract and normalized-navigation roles; short by design.

manual_audit_2026_09_10.limitation: The manual repository map was performed through the connected GitHub repository because the execution sandbox could not clone github.com. The upgraded audit script should be run in CI or a repository checkout to produce exact project-wide depth counts.

audit_script_scope: By default scans structured JSON under data/ and knowledge/ with role-aware scoring; large country datasets are opt-in.
routing_rule: A deep record is useful only when a reader can reach it from the canonical navigation and then follow source, relationship and research trails without entering a parallel competing application.
